Scarlett O'Hara.look: Sixteen, small and slender, dark hair piled high, green eyes, in a green sprigged muslin dress with a wide sash, a fan snapping open and shut.

Ashley Wilkes.look: Tall, slim, late twenties, pale blond hair and grey eyes, in a grey broadcloth coat; quiet, with a faint smile.

Rhett Butler.look: Tall, heavy-shouldered, mid-thirties, black hair, a small black moustache, swarthy, in a black suit; mocking eyes.

Charles Hamilton.look: A shy boy of twenty, brown curls, soft brown eyes, flushed, in a new grey coat too formal for a barbecue.

Melanie Hamilton.look: Small and frail, seventeen, heart-shaped face, brown eyes too large for it, dark hair in a net, grey organdie dress.

Honey Wilkes.look: A thin blonde girl with lashless pale eyes and a petulant mouth, in pink, talking fast.

India Wilkes.look: Plain, colourless, with pale lashes and a set jaw, hair drawn tight, in a dull blue dress.

Stuart Tarleton.look: Nineteen, six feet two, red hair, sunburnt, long legs in riding boots, hot-tempered.

Brent Tarleton.look: Stuart's twin, the same red hair and sunburn, a shade quieter, always at his brother's heels.

Jim Tarleton.look: A big, loud, red-faced planter in his fifties, the twins' father, whiskey glass in hand.

Mr. McRae.look: A deaf old gentleman from Fayetteville, white-haired, with a cane, shouting because he cannot hear himself.

Cathleen Calvert.look: A pretty, fair, gossipy girl of sixteen in a yellow dress.

scenes.title: The lawn: Charles proposes, the men talk war, Rhett speaks
scenes.place: The back lawn of Twelve Oaks under the great oaks, benches and the arbor, the barbecue pits smoking, a warm April noon in 1861.

scenes.title: The library: Scarlett and Ashley, Rhett on the sofa
scenes.place: The library at Twelve Oaks in semidarkness, blinds drawn against the sun, tall bookcases, a high-backed sofa, a little table with a china rose-bowl; early afternoon.

scenes.title: The hall and the bench: the girls upstairs, Charles and the news from Lincoln
scenes.place: The silent upper hall and front steps of Twelve Oaks in the drowsy afternoon, then a bench on the lawn; a rider has just come up the drive.
